title: Why Your Brain Can't Feel Exponential Growth
subtitle: Fold a paper 42 times and it reaches the Moon. Your gut says 'a few inches.' That gap explains pandemics, compound interest, and viral everything.
hook: A sheet of paper is ~0.1mm thick. Fold it in half 42 times and it would reach the Moon. Your gut is screaming that's impossible — and that scream is the single most expensive blind spot in human reasoning. We think in straight lines; reality often moves in curves that explode. Pandemics, compound interest, viral growth, climate — all run on exponentials our intuition simply cannot feel. Today: how to override the blind spot.

sections.heading: Linear brain, exponential world
sections.body: Our intuition is **linear**: add the same amount each step (1, 2, 3, 4…). Exponentials **multiply** each step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16…). For a while they look similar — which lulls you — then the exponential detonates. Thirty linear steps of +1 gets you to 30. Thirty exponential steps of ×2 gets you to over a *billion*. Same number of steps, unimaginably different destinations.

sections.caption: Linear and exponential start close, then diverge violently. The 'nothing's happening… wait, WHAT' feeling is the trap.

sections.label: The tricks to override it
sections.body: You can't feel exponentials, so use tools. Doubling time: ask 'how long to double?' and count doublings — each one matches everything that came before it *combined*. Rule of 72: 72 ÷ growth-rate ≈ years to double (from the compounding lesson!). Watch the rate, not the level: in exponential processes, today's small number plus a steady growth rate tells you tomorrow's scary one.

sections.label: It cuts both ways
sections.body: Exponential growth builds fortunes (compounding) and crises (runaway debt, unchecked spread). Exponential *decay* is just as sneaky — skills, machines, and advantages erode faster than they feel like they should. The lesson isn't 'exponentials are good' — it's 'when something compounds, your gut will be wrong, so reach for the math.'

sections.caption: 3Blue1Brown on exponential growth and why our intuition fails (with a timely example).

takeaways: Intuition is **linear** (add); many real processes are **exponential** (multiply).
They look similar early, then the exponential **explodes** — that's the trap.
30 steps of +1 → 30; 30 steps of ×2 → over a billion.
Override with **doubling time**, the **Rule of 72**, and watching the **growth rate**.
It cuts both ways — growth *and* decay compound faster than they feel.
